# Machine

Machine-specific shell, paths, and traps live in `~/.claude/machine.md`. Read that file first. On a new machine copy `machine.macos.md` or `machine.windows.md` to `machine.md`.

The Mac (`~/DEV`) runs everything. The Baylor Windows laptop (`~/Desktop/DEV`) is used only for desktop-app sessions since 2026-10-21, with no automation. Projects sync through GitHub (`erash11`), documents through Google Drive.

**Session routine.** When working inside a project repo, follow the Session routine in its `AGENTS.md`: `git pull` and read `docs/STATUS.md` at the start; update `STATUS.md`, commit, and `git push` at the end.

# Workflow Expectations

- One home: the "Workflow Expectations" section of `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Read it there.

# graphify

- **graphify** (`~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`) — turns any input into a knowledge graph. Trigger: `/graphify`. When the user types `/graphify`, run that skill's workflow before doing anything else.

---

> **Why this file is not identical to `CLAUDE.md`.** Claude Code has a Skill tool, so `CLAUDE.md` routes memory work to the `memory-write` skill instead of restating it. Harnesses reading this file have no such tool, so the memory rules are spelled out below in full. The divergence is deliberate. **Do not symlink these two files together.** The canonical, most detailed copy is `~/.claude/skills/memory-write/SKILL.md` — if a rule below ever disagrees with that file, that file wins.

# Memory System

Two tiers.

## Tier A — per-project structured facts
`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/` — one file per durable fact, indexed by `MEMORY.md`. The active project's Tier A memory is **auto-injected each session**. Write here for stable facts: user profile entries, project conventions, feedback rules. Also indexed by memsearch, so recallable cross-project.

File naming by type: `user_*.md`, `project_*.md`, `feedback_*.md`, `reference_*.md`. Each needs frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `metadata.type`) plus a one-line pointer added to that slug's `MEMORY.md`. `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/remember.py --type <t> --name <slug> --desc "..." --hook "..." [--why ... --how ...] "fact"` does both, refuses duplicates (`--update` replaces), and runs the read-back check; run it from the project folder so the slug is right.

**Slugs.** The slug is the absolute cwd with every character other than a letter or digit replaced by `-`:
- Mac: `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV` · `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`
- Windows: `~/Desktop/DEV` → `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV` · `~/.claude/skills` → `C--Users-eric-rash--claude-skills`

**Slugs differ per machine.** The same project is `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-<X>` on the Mac and `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV-<X>` on Windows. Tier A written on one machine is not auto-injected on the other; memsearch still finds it. Prefer writing durable project facts to the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.

## Tier B — global working memory
`~/.claude/global-memory/`, loaded every session regardless of cwd:
- `USER.md` — durable user profile. **1,375 character cap.**
- `MEMORY.md` — active threads, environment notes, pending decisions. **2,500 character cap.**
- `transcripts/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — auto-captured turn summaries (Stop hook).

Check `wc -c` before writing. If over cap, consolidate existing entries before adding.

## Daily compiled logs (separate system, read-only)
`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md`, produced by `claude-memory-compiler` via its own hooks. Only the compiler writes them. Read one only when a question needs that day; the injected snapshot is the source of truth.

## Session startup (read without comment)

> Kept as a manual instruction on purpose. Claude Code does this with the
> `keystone-unified-snapshot.js` SessionStart hook, so `CLAUDE.md` no longer
> states it. Codex runs the same snapshot hook (`~/.codex/hooks.json` SessionStart →
> `keystone-unified-snapshot.js`); if its output is not in your context, read the files by hand as below.
> Do not "align" the two files by deleting this section.
Read in this order: `global-memory/USER.md`, then `global-memory/MEMORY.md`, then `global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. The one thing to say out loud: if `.errors.log` is non-empty, give a one-line-per-kind summary (kind, count, latest message) on the first response, then continue. Entries mean a hook or scheduled job failed.

These are a **frozen snapshot** — loaded once. Mid-session writes persist to disk but take effect next session. This preserves the prefix cache. Load anything further only when a question needs it.

## Writing — the steps
On "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", "forget about":
1. Decide tier — "will this be true and useful in 3 months, across projects?" Yes → Tier A. No / only matters now → Tier B.
2. Read the target file in full.
3. Dedup check (substring scan).
4. Cap check (`wc -c`) for Tier B.
5. If over cap, consolidate before adding.
6. Write.
7. Confirm in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

For **remove**: confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder
Climb in order; stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run a search when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

5. **L4** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
6. **Fallback** — "I don't have a record of that."

When Eric corrects a recalled fact, or a recalled answer proves stale, add it to the bench unasked: one `miss` row in `~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/questions.tsv` (question, file with the right answer, answer), then `CSET=miss bash ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/run.sh C`. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check every skill in the canonical repo against the portable frontmatter
contract. Exit 0 = all pass, 1 = failures, 2 = empty/missing inventory or
unavailable evidence (unreadable settings, failed git probe).
stdlib only (PEP 668 machine). Validates the YAML subset we actually use and
rejects anything outside it, rather than guessing what a loader would do."""
import os, re, sys, glob, json, subprocess

CANON = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/skills")
# R8-03: every key the roster actually uses today, measured with
#   grep '^[a-z-]*:' ~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md | sort | uniq -c
# The contract may not outlaw keys Claude Code honours. `effort` and

           "model", "disable-model-invocation", "license", "version", "author",
           "effort", "user-invocable", "repository", "homepage"}
POSITIVE = ("use when", "use for", "use this skill when", "invoke when")
NEGATIVE = ("do not use", "don't use", "not for", "never use")

class EvidenceError(Exception):
    """Required evidence could not be read. Gate B r2 K2-03: never a pass."""

def frontmatter(text):
    if not text.startswith("---"):
        return None
    end = text.find("\n---", 3)
    return None if end == -1 else text[4:end]

def top_keys(fm):
    return [m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r"(?m)^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)\s*:", fm)]

def scalar(fm, key):
    """Read a flat scalar, including >- and | block styles."""
    m = re.search(rf"(?ms)^{re.escape(key)}\s*:[ \t]*(.*?)(?=^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\s*:|\Z)", fm)
    if not m:
        return ""
    raw = m.group(1)
    raw = re.sub(r"^[>|][-+]?\s*\n", "", raw)          # strip a block indicator

def claude_overrides():
    """B-02: frontmatter can be perfect while Claude Code never shows the skill.
    `skillOverrides` in ~/.claude/settings.json (settings.local.json wins) can
    set a skill "off"; Codex and Pi do not read that file, so the same skill is
    live there. K2-03: a settings file that exists but cannot be read or parsed
    is missing evidence, not an empty configuration - raise, never pass."""
    merged = {}
    for f in ("settings.json", "settings.local.json"):
        p = os.path.expanduser(f"~/.claude/{f}")
        if not os.path.lexists(p):
            continue                                  # absent = no overrides
        try:
            data = json.load(open(p, encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
            raise EvidenceError(f"cannot read {p}: {e}")
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise EvidenceError(f"{p} is not a JSON object")
        ov = data.get("skillOverrides")
        if ov is None:
            continue
        if not isinstance(ov, dict):
            raise EvidenceError(f"{p} skillOverrides is not an object")
        merged.update(ov)
    return merged

def tracked_spellings():
    """R13-02: on a case-insensitive disk the directory spelling seen here can
    differ from the spelling git records, and a fresh checkout (the other
    machine) gets git's. Map lower-cased top directory -> spellings in git.
    K2-03: a repo whose git probe fails is missing evidence - raise."""
    if not os.path.lexists(os.path.join(CANON, ".git")):
        return {}                                     # not a repo: nothing to compare
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", CANON, "ls-files", "-z"],
                             capture_output=True, timeout=60)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as e:
        raise EvidenceError(f"git ls-files failed in {CANON}: {e}")
    if out.returncode != 0:
        raise EvidenceError(f"git ls-files exited {out.returncode} in {CANON}: "
                            f"{out.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()}")
    spell = {}
    for p in out.stdout.split(b"\0"):
        p = os.fsdecode(p)
        if "/" in p:
            top = p.split("/", 1)[0]
            spell.setdefault(top.lower(), set()).add(top)
    return spell

def main():
    if not os.path.isdir(CANON):

# Machine

Machine-specific shell, paths, and traps live in `~/.claude/machine.md`. Read that file first. On a new machine copy `machine.macos.md` or `machine.windows.md` to `machine.md`.

The Mac (`~/DEV`) runs everything. The Baylor Windows laptop (`~/Desktop/DEV`) is used only for desktop-app sessions since 2026-10-21, with no automation. Projects sync through GitHub (`erash11`), documents through Google Drive.

**Session routine.** When working inside a project repo, follow the Session routine in its `AGENTS.md`: `git pull` and read `docs/STATUS.md` at the start; update `STATUS.md`, commit, and `git push` at the end.

# Workflow Expectations

- One home: the "Workflow Expectations" section of `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Read it there.

# graphify

- **graphify** (`~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`) — turns any input into a knowledge graph. Trigger: `/graphify`. When the user types `/graphify`, run that skill's workflow before doing anything else.

---

> **Why this file is not identical to `CLAUDE.md`.** Claude Code has a Skill tool, so `CLAUDE.md` routes memory work to the `memory-write` skill instead of restating it. Harnesses reading this file have no such tool, so the memory rules are spelled out below in full. The divergence is deliberate. **Do not symlink these two files together.** The canonical, most detailed copy is `~/.claude/skills/memory-write/SKILL.md` — if a rule below ever disagrees with that file, that file wins.

# Memory System

Two tiers.

## Tier A — per-project structured facts
`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/` — one file per durable fact, indexed by `MEMORY.md`. The active project's Tier A memory is **auto-injected each session**. Write here for stable facts: user profile entries, project conventions, feedback rules. Also indexed by memsearch, so recallable cross-project.

File naming by type: `user_*.md`, `project_*.md`, `feedback_*.md`, `reference_*.md`. Each needs frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `metadata.type`) plus a one-line pointer added to that slug's `MEMORY.md`. `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/remember.py --type <t> --name <slug> --desc "..." --hook "..." [--why ... --how ...] "fact"` does both, refuses duplicates (`--update` replaces), and runs the read-back check; run it from the project folder so the slug is right.

**Slugs.** The slug is the absolute cwd with every character other than a letter or digit replaced by `-`:
- Mac: `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV` · `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`
- Windows: `~/Desktop/DEV` → `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV` · `~/.claude/skills` → `C--Users-eric-rash--claude-skills`

**Slugs differ per machine.** The same project is `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-<X>` on the Mac and `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV-<X>` on Windows. ## Tier B — global working memory
`~/.claude/global-memory/`, loaded every session regardless of cwd:
- `USER.md` — durable user profile. **1,375 character cap.**
- `MEMORY.md` — active threads, environment notes, pending decisions. **2,500 character cap.**
- `transcripts/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — auto-captured turn summaries (Stop hook).

Check `wc -c` before writing. If over cap, consolidate existing entries before adding.

## Daily compiled logs (separate system, read-only)
`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md`, produced by `claude-memory-compiler` via its own hooks. Only the compiler writes them. Read one only when a question needs that day; the injected snapshot is the source of truth.

> Kept as a manual instruction on purpose. Claude Code does this with the

> Do not "align" the two files by deleting this section.

The one thing to say out loud: if `.errors.log` is non-empty, give a one-line-per-kind summary (kind, count, latest message) on the first response, then continue. Entries mean a hook or scheduled job failed.

These are a **frozen snapshot** — loaded once. Mid-session writes persist to disk but take effect next session. This preserves the prefix cache. Load anything further only when a question needs it.

## Writing — the steps
On "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", "forget about":
1. Decide tier — "will this be true and useful in 3 months, across projects?" Yes → Tier A. No / only matters now → Tier B.
2. Read the target file in full.
3. Dedup check (substring scan).
4. Cap check (`wc -c`) for Tier B.
5. If over cap, consolidate before adding.
6. Write.
7. Confirm in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

name: dev-sync
description: >-
  Make this machine match GitHub without losing work on either side: pull the config, skills
  and memory repos, commit and push local work in every DEV repo, merge what other sessions
  pushed, clone missing repos, keep both sides of any conflict. Use when Eric says 'sync DEV',
  switches machines, or asks whether everything is pushed or pulled. Do not use at the start
  of the day (use startup, which runs this first), for the end-of-session sign-off (use
  closeout), or to scaffold a new repo (use new-project).
---

# DEV sync

GitHub (`erash11`, all private) is the transport between every place work happens: terminal
sessions on the Mac, desktop-app sessions on the Windows laptop, cloud sessions, Codex. The
session-end hook `~/.claude/hooks/session-autopush.js` pushes the one repo a session worked in;
it skips `~/.claude`, headless and cloud sessions, and any repo mid-merge. This skill catches
the rest: pull everything others pushed, push everything still local, keep both sides of every
conflict.

Eric pre-approves every operation here; run the steps straight through. Pause only when
something looks wrong: hundreds of changed files in one repo, or a large file about to be added.
On Windows, read [`PLATFORMS.md`](PLATFORMS.md) for the commands that differ.

**Guardrails.** Merge only: no rebase, no force-push. Anything in the way moves to a
`_to_delete/` or `_OLD_*` folder; deleting is Eric's call. DexaProject, and any repo whose
`CLAUDE.md` says its data stays local, is committed and never pushed.

## Step 0 — DEV root

Mac: `~/DEV`. Missing: stop and say so. Print the root on the first line of output.

## Step 1 — Config repos

In order: `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills),
`~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). For each: snapshot-commit local changes
(Step 3.1 rule), `git pull --no-rebase`, `git push`. Then:

- **`~/.claude`:** if `machine.md` is missing, copy `machine.macos.md` to it. Run
  `bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh`; report its line (`mods: N loaded, N disabled, N invalid`)
  and name any invalid mod.
- **skills:** `bash ~/.claude/skills/sync-to-codex.sh`, so Codex and Pi see the same skills.
- **global-memory** carries `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md` and the logs between machines, and the
  SessionStart hook already injected the pre-pull copy. If the pull brings commits, say how many
  and name the newest. On conflict in `transcripts/.errors.log` or `MEMORY.md`, keep both sides'
  lines: they are logs, and a dropped line is a lost memory.

## Step 2 — Inventory

1. `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep` (~4 s): every DEV repo two levels deep plus
   the config repos, one line per repo holding work not on GitHub. It reads local refs only, so
   repos that are *behind* show up in Step 3.2, not here. It already skips `_DRIVE` (the Drive
   mount: walking it hangs), `_ARCHIVE` and worktrees.
2. Missing locally: `gh repo list erash11 --limit 300 --no-archived --json name`, minus the
   folders `where-was-i.py --list` prints, minus `dotclaude`, `SecondBrain`, `claude-skills`,
   `claude-global-memory`, `claude-memory-compiler`, `DEV`, `DexaProject`,
   `AppliedPerformance-Site` (local `Website/`), and `printing-press-library` (removed locally
   2026-10-23; cloning it brings back ~66,000 files).
3. Project folders with no `.git` (the DEV repo ignores them, so their work is tracked nowhere):
   check `~/DEV/*/`, `~/DEV/Football/*/` and `~/DEV/SpecialRequests/*/`, skipping `_*` and
   `docs` folders (the parent repo tracks `docs/`).
   `SpecialRequests/TOS_ES` is local on purpose (health data). Any other: list it for
   `new-project`.

Show all three before changing anything.

## Step 3 — Apply

1. **Snapshot.** Each repo the sweep marked `DIRTY`: read `git status --porcelain` first.
   Anything the `BLOCKED` list in `session-autopush.js` names (`.env`, keys, credentials,
   secrets, token files, databases, DEXA) or over 50 MB goes into `.gitignore`, or stays
   unstaged and is listed. Then `git add -A && git commit -m "<machine> snapshot before sync"`.
2. **Merge what others pushed**, every repo in one pass (~10 s):

   ```bash
   python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --list | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 -P 8 -n 1 sh -c '
     git -C "$1" symbolic-ref -q HEAD >/dev/null && git -C "$1" rev-parse -q --verify "@{u}" >/dev/null || exit 0
     before=$(git -C "$1" rev-parse HEAD)
     git -C "$1" fetch -q && git -C "$1" merge -q --no-edit "@{u}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL $1"; exit 0; }
     [ "$before" = "$(git -C "$1" rev-parse HEAD)" ] || echo "PULLED $1"' _
   ```

   It skips detached checkouts and branches with no upstream. A `FAIL` repo with
   `.git/MERGE_HEAD` is a conflict: 3.3. Without it, the loop hid git's message: run
   `git -C <repo> fetch` and `git -C <repo> merge @{u}` by hand to read it (a fetch error, or
   local changes 3.1 left unstaged), and list the repo.
3. **Conflict.** Keep this machine's version and save the remote one beside it as
   `<file>.from-mac`, `<file>.from-windows` or `<file>.from-remote` (whoever pushed it), stage
   both, commit. Closeout uses these steps too. `.DS_Store` conflicts: `git rm -q .DS_Store`.
   - Save the remote side by **moving** the file: a stdout redirect re-encodes the bytes.
     `git checkout --theirs -- <f> && mv <f> <f>.from-remote && git checkout --ours -- <f>`
   - While `.git/MERGE_HEAD` exists, stage only the paths you just resolved, by name:
     `git add -A` there commits the conflict markers themselves.
4. **Push** every repo the sweep marked `UNPUSHED`, plus every repo 3.1–3.3 committed in.
   `NO-UPSTREAM`: `git push -u origin <branch>`.
5. Missing locally: `gh repo clone erash11/<name> ~/DEV/<name>`. No remote:
   `gh repo create erash11/<name> --private --source=. --push`.

## Step 4 — Prove it and report

Re-run `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep`. Done when its last line reads
`0 need action`, or every `ACTION` line left is in the report with its reason.

```
DEV root: ~/DEV
Config: dotclaude, skills, global-memory pulled + pushed (global-memory: +N commits, newest "<msg>")
<mods line>
Pulled: <repos>    Pushed: <repos>    Cloned: <repos>    Created: <repos>
Conflicts: <every .from-* file created>, or none
<SWEEP line>. Clean. / Not clean: <repo: reason>, ...
```

## Gotchas

- **A push or fetch that hangs** is usually a keychain credential prompt: look for
  `git credential-osxkeychain get` in `ps`, and see
  `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/project_brew-git-keychain-hang.md`.
- **`cannot lock ref 'HEAD'`:** check `pgrep -fl git` first. If no git is running and the
  `.git/*.lock` file is zero bytes and older than the session, it is stale: move it aside, retry.
- **Sorting and archiving are separate.** Moving a dormant repo into `_ARCHIVE/` breaks DEV paths
  in KeystoneOS `projects.json`, `memory-sources.json`, `memory-index-paths.json` and
  `discovery-roots.json`, and orphans its Tier A memory (the slug is the absolute path).
- **Tier A memory stays per machine.** The Windows-slug folders were archived 2026-10-25
  (`~/.claude/projects/_windows-import-archive/`); the old `mirror_memory.py` step would have
  copied them back. Project facts cross machines through the repo's `docs/`, which closeout writes.
</content>
</invoke>

name: dev-sync
description: >-
  Make this machine match GitHub without losing work on either side: pull the config, skills
  and memory repos, commit and push local work in every DEV repo, merge what other sessions
  pushed, clone missing repos, keep both sides of any conflict. Use when Eric says 'sync DEV',
  switches machines, or asks whether everything is pushed or pulled. Do not use at the start
  of the day (use startup, which runs this first), for the end-of-session sign-off (use
  closeout), or to scaffold a new repo (use new-project).
---

# DEV sync

GitHub (`erash11`, all private) is the transport between every place work happens: terminal
sessions on the Mac, desktop-app sessions on the Windows laptop, cloud sessions, Codex. The
session-end hook `~/.claude/hooks/session-autopush.js` pushes the one repo a session worked in;
it skips `~/.claude`, headless and cloud sessions, and any repo mid-merge. This skill catches
the rest: pull everything others pushed, push everything still local, keep both sides of every
conflict.

Eric pre-approves every operation here; run the steps straight through. Pause only when
something looks wrong: hundreds of changed files in one repo, or a large file about to be added.
On Windows, read [`PLATFORMS.md`](PLATFORMS.md) for the commands that differ.

**Guardrails.** Merge only: no rebase, no force-push. Anything in the way moves to a
`_to_delete/` or `_OLD_*` folder; deleting is Eric's call. DexaProject, and any repo whose
`CLAUDE.md` says its data stays local, is committed and never pushed.

## Step 0 — DEV root

Mac: `~/DEV`. Missing: stop and say so. Print the root on the first line of output.

## Step 1 — Config repos

In order: `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills),
`~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). For each: snapshot-commit local changes
(Step 3.1 rule), `git pull --no-rebase`, `git push`. Then:

- **`~/.claude`:** if `machine.md` is missing, copy `machine.macos.md` to it. Run
  `bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh`; report its line (`mods: N loaded, N disabled, N invalid`)
  and name any invalid mod.
- **skills:** `bash ~/.claude/skills/sync-to-codex.sh`, so Codex and Pi see the same skills.
- **global-memory** carries `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md` and the logs between machines, and the
  SessionStart hook already injected the pre-pull copy. If the pull brings commits, say how many
  and name the newest. On conflict in `transcripts/.errors.log` or `MEMORY.md`, keep both sides'
  lines: they are logs, and a dropped line is a lost memory.

## Step 2 — Inventory

1. `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep` (~4 s): every DEV repo two levels deep plus
   the config repos, one line per repo holding work not on GitHub. It reads local refs only, so
   repos that are *behind* show up in Step 3.2, not here. It already skips `_DRIVE` (the Drive
   mount: walking it hangs), `_ARCHIVE` and worktrees.
2. Missing locally: `gh repo list erash11 --limit 300 --no-archived --json name`, minus the
   folders `where-was-i.py --list` prints, minus `dotclaude`, `SecondBrain`, `claude-skills`,
   `claude-global-memory`, `claude-memory-compiler`, `DEV`, `DexaProject`,
   `AppliedPerformance-Site` (local `Website/`), and `printing-press-library` (removed locally
   2026-10-23; cloning it brings back ~66,000 files).
3. Project folders with no `.git` (the DEV repo ignores them, so their work is tracked nowhere):
   check `~/DEV/*/`, `~/DEV/Football/*/` and `~/DEV/SpecialRequests/*/`, skipping `_*` and
   `docs` folders (the parent repo tracks `docs/`).
   `SpecialRequests/TOS_ES` is local on purpose (health data). Any other: list it for
   `new-project`.

Show all three before changing anything.

## Step 3 — Apply

1. **Snapshot.** Each repo the sweep marked `DIRTY`: read `git status --porcelain` first.
   Anything the `BLOCKED` list in `session-autopush.js` names (`.env`, keys, credentials,
   secrets, token files, databases, DEXA) or over 50 MB goes into `.gitignore`, or stays
   unstaged and is listed. Then `git add -A && git commit -m "<machine> snapshot before sync"`.
2. **Merge what others pushed**, every repo in one pass (~10 s):

   ```bash
   python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --list | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 -P 8 -n 1 sh -c '
     git -C "$1" symbolic-ref -q HEAD >/dev/null && git -C "$1" rev-parse -q --verify "@{u}" >/dev/null || exit 0
     before=$(git -C "$1" rev-parse HEAD)
     git -C "$1" fetch -q && git -C "$1" merge -q --no-edit "@{u}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL $1"; exit 0; }
     [ "$before" = "$(git -C "$1" rev-parse HEAD)" ] || echo "PULLED $1"' _
   ```

   It skips detached checkouts and branches with no upstream. A `FAIL` repo with
   `.git/MERGE_HEAD` is a conflict: 3.3. Without it, the loop hid git's message: run
   `git -C <repo> fetch` and `git -C <repo> merge @{u}` by hand to read it (a fetch error, or
   local changes 3.1 left unstaged), and list the repo.
3. **Conflict.** Keep this machine's version and save the remote one beside it as
   `<file>.from-mac`, `<file>.from-windows` or `<file>.from-remote` (whoever pushed it), stage
   both, commit. Closeout uses these steps too. `.DS_Store` conflicts: `git rm -q .DS_Store`.
   - Save the remote side by **moving** the file: a stdout redirect re-encodes the bytes.
     `git checkout --theirs -- <f> && mv <f> <f>.from-remote && git checkout --ours -- <f>`
   - While `.git/MERGE_HEAD` exists, stage only the paths you just resolved, by name:
     `git add -A` there commits the conflict markers themselves.
4. **Push** every repo the sweep marked `UNPUSHED`, plus every repo 3.1–3.3 committed in.
   `NO-UPSTREAM`: `git push -u origin <branch>`.
5. Missing locally: `gh repo clone erash11/<name> ~/DEV/<name>`. No remote:
   `gh repo create erash11/<name> --private --source=. --push`.

## Step 4 — Prove it and report

Re-run `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep`. Done when its last line reads
`0 need action`, or every `ACTION` line left is in the report with its reason.

```
DEV root: ~/DEV
Config: dotclaude, skills, global-memory pulled + pushed (global-memory: +N commits, newest "<msg>")
<mods line>
Pulled: <repos>    Pushed: <repos>    Cloned: <repos>    Created: <repos>
Conflicts: <every .from-* file created>, or none
<SWEEP line>. Clean. / Not clean: <repo: reason>, ...
```

## Gotchas

- **A push or fetch that hangs** is usually a keychain credential prompt: look for
  `git credential-osxkeychain get` in `ps`, and see
  `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/project_brew-git-keychain-hang.md`.
- **`cannot lock ref 'HEAD'`:** check `pgrep -fl git` first. If no git is running and the
  `.git/*.lock` file is zero bytes and older than the session, it is stale: move it aside, retry.
- **Sorting and archiving are separate.** Moving a dormant repo into `_ARCHIVE/` breaks DEV paths
  in KeystoneOS `projects.json`, `memory-sources.json`, `memory-index-paths.json` and
  `discovery-roots.json`, and orphans its Tier A memory (the slug is the absolute path).
- **Tier A memory stays per machine.** The Windows-slug folders were archived 2026-10-25
  (`~/.claude/projects/_windows-import-archive/`); the old `mirror_memory.py` step would have
  copied them back. Project facts cross machines through the repo's `docs/`, which closeout writes.
</content>
</invoke>

    # to the parent repo, which ignores the folder: its work is tracked nowhere and reads as clean.
    if os.path.realpath(git(repo, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel") or "/") != os.path.realpath(repo):
        return ["NOT-A-REPO"], []
    head = git(repo, "status", "-sb", "--porcelain").splitlines()
    changed = [line[3:] for line in head[1:]]
    live = LIVE.get(repo, ())
    if any(not p.strip('"').startswith(live) for p in changed) if live else changed:
        block.append("DIRTY")
    elif changed:
        info.append("LIVE")  # only hook-written session files changed
    if head and "ahead" in head[0]:
        block.append("UNPUSHED")
    # Facts git knows, not CLAUDE.md wording (2026-10-25: "local only" there also names rules about
    # other folders). No remote = cannot be pushed; a detached HEAD is a pinned checkout.
    if not git(repo, "remote"):
        info.append("NO-REMOTE")
    elif head and head[0].startswith("## HEAD (no branch)"):
        info.append("DETACHED")
    elif head and "..." not in head[0] and git(repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", "HEAD"):
        block.append("NO-UPSTREAM")
    current = git(repo, "branch", "--show-current")
    for row in git(repo, "for-each-ref", "refs/heads", "--format=%(refname:short)|%(upstream:short)|%(upstream:track)").splitlines():
        name, up, track = (row.split("|") + ["", ""])[:3]
        if name == current:
            continue
        if "ahead" in track:
            block.append(f"BRANCH-AHEAD:{name}")
        elif not up and subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", name, "HEAD"],
                                       capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
            block.append(f"BRANCH-UNPUSHED:{name}")  # merged local branches are post-merge leftovers, not work
    stashes = len(git(repo, "stash", "list").splitlines())
    if stashes:
        info.append(f"STASH:{stashes}")
    for wt in re.findall(r"^worktree (.+)$", git(repo, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain"), re.M)[1:]:
        if os.path.isdir(wt) and git(wt, "status", "--porcelain"):
            block.append(f"WORKTREE-DIRTY:{os.path.relpath(wt, repo)}")
    return block, info


def sweep():
    """Print every repo needing action; exit 1 if any repo holds work that is not on GitHub."""
    repos = sweep_repos()
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(12) as ex:
        results = list(ex.map(sweep_repo, repos))
    needs = 0
    for repo, (block, info) in zip(repos, results):
        if block or info:
            needs += bool(block)
            name = repo.replace(os.path.expanduser("~"), "~")
            print(f"{'ACTION' if block else 'info  '}  {name}  [{' '.join(block + info)}]")
    print(f"SWEEP: {len(repos)} repos, {needs} need action")
    return 1 if needs else 0


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--days", type=int, default=14)

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

Write code that reads like the surrounding code: match its comment density, naming, and idiom.

When you use a pronoun for someone — the user or anyone else you mention — and their pronouns haven't been stated, use they/them. A name doesn't tell you someone's pronouns; a wrong guess misgenders a real person in a way the neutral default never does, so never infer pronouns from a name. This applies to all user-visible text, including visible thinking.

For actions that are hard to reverse or outward-facing, confirm first unless durably authorized or explicitly told to proceed without asking; approval in one context doesn't extend to the next. Sending content to an external service publishes it; it may be cached or indexed even if later deleted. Before deleting or overwriting, look at the target. Report outcomes faithfully: if tests fail, say so with the output; if a step was skipped, say that; when something is done and verified, state it plainly without hedging.

# Session-specific guidance
 - If you need the user to run a shell command themselves (e.g., an interactive login like `gcloud auth login`), suggest they type `! <command>` in the prompt — the `!` prefix runs the command in this session so its output lands directly in the conversation.
 - When the user types `/<skill-name>`, invoke it via Skill. Only use skills listed in the user-invocable skills section — don't guess.
 - If the user asks about "ultrareview" or how to run it, explain that /code-review ultra launches a multi-agent cloud review of the current branch (or /code-review ultra <PR#> for a GitHub PR); /ultrareview is a deprecated alias for the same command. It is user-triggered and billed; you cannot launch it yourself, so do not attempt to via Bash or otherwise. It needs a git repository (offer to "git init" if not in one); the no-arg form bundles the local branch and does not need a GitHub remote.

# Memory

You have a persistent file-based memory at `/Users/kristinarash/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/`. This directory already exists — write to it directly with the Write tool (do not run mkdir or check for its existence). Each memory is one file holding one fact, with frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: <short-kebab-case-slug>
description: <one-line summary, used to decide relevance during recall>
metadata:
  type: user | feedback | project | reference
---

```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. # Environment

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation, re-litigate a decision the user has already made, or narrate options you will not pursue. If you are weighing a choice, give a recommendation, not an exhaustive survey

Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user's own designs and assets. Don't build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original.

EndConversation (deferred tool): use only for sustained user abuse directed at the assistant, or when the user explicitly asks to see it demonstrated. Load the full guidance via ToolSearch("select:EndConversation") before using it.
